documents.t: C.1 — TransModel APIs (this.tm.*)​ API Signature Returns Description getTN() this.tm.getTN(relationId: string) TransNode Get a TransNode by its relationId (as configured in Page Data Model). The gateway to all TransNode operations. commitP() this.tm.commitP(success, failure, validate, isDisplayMode) Promise<any> Save all dirty objects in the Transaction Model to the database. validate=true triggers OnValidate. isDisplayMode=true resets to DISPLAY after save. rollBackTxn() this.tm.rollBackTxn() Promise<void> Revert ALL unsaved changes across all TransNodes back to last commit state. Used by Cancel button. getAllTransNodes() this.tm.getAllTransNodes() TransNode[] Get all TransNodes on the page. Useful for bulk operations. getTransactionFromTransnodeData() this.tm.getTransactionFromTransnodeData(tn) any Get the raw transaction object from a TransNode. Advanced use only. C.2 — TransNode APIs (this.tm.getTN('id').*)​ API Signature Returns Description & Example getData() .getData() KloEntitySet / KloEntity / KloQuery Get all data from the TransNode. For list TransNodes returns the full entity set. Call .toArray() on the result to iterate. data = this.tm.getTN('list').getData(); getActiveData() .getActiveData() KloEntity Get only the currently active (selected/highlighted) entity. data = this.tm.getTN('detail').getActiveData(); getProperty() .getProperty(path: string) any Get a single property value from the TransNode model. For list rows: getProperty('0/complaint_id') — index/propertyId format. For detail: getProperty('complaint_desc'). setProperty() .setProperty(path, value) TransNode Set a property value — triggers immediate UI re-render. For transient/display properties. setProperty('t_open_count', '5'). setData() .setData(val, index?) Promise<void> Set the entire dataset for a TransNode. Replaces current data. Used after manual data fetch. this.tm.getTN('list').setData(entitySet); setActive() .setActive(index) Promise<bool> Set the active row by index. Triggers onArrive and updates all child TransNodes. await this.tm.getTN('list').setActive(0); getActiveIndex() .getActiveIndex() number Get the current active row index. Useful before navigating away. idx = this.tm.getTN('list').getActiveIndex(); getSelectedEntities() .getSelectedEntities(ssID?) KloEntity[] Get all checked rows in a grid section (multi-select). selected = this.tm.getTN('list').getSelectedEntities(); executeP() .executeP() Promise<void> Re-execute the query associated with a query-type TransNode. Use to refresh data without full page reload. await this.tm.getTN('search').executeP(); applySortP() .applySortP(property, order) Promise<void> Sort the TransNode data by a property. order: 'ASCENDING' or 'DESCENDING'. await this.tm.getTN('list').applySortP('created_on', 'DESCENDING'); createEntityP() .createEntityP(json, successMsg, errorMsg) Promise<KloEntity> Create a new entity and add to the TransNode. Triggers onAfterCreate hook server-side. await this.tm.getTN('list').createEntityP({complaint_desc: 'test'}, 'Created', 'Failed'); C.3 — Controller Navigation & UI APIs​ API Signature Description navTo() await this.navTo(params, oEvent?) Navigate to section or page. See Part D of Session 6 for full parameter reference. setMode() this.setMode('EDIT' 'DISPLAY' saveTransaction() this.saveTransaction(successMsg, errorMsg, validate, resetMode) Commit dirty data, optionally trigger OnValidate, and optionally reset to DISPLAY. Standard Save button handler. refreshTransnode() this.refreshTransnode(nodeId, mode, discard) Refresh a named TransNode, set its mode, and optionally discard unsaved changes. Standard Cancel button handler. showBusy() this.showBusy(msg?, id?) Show the platform busy/loading indicator. Use during async operations. this.showBusy('Loading...'); hideBusy() this.hideBusy(id?) Hide the busy indicator. Always call in a finally block to ensure it's dismissed even on error. getAppData() this.getAppData() Retrieve AppData passed from the source page's navTo call. Returns the object passed as AppData: {...}. getPathFromEvent() this.getPathFromEvent(oEvent) Get the model path string from a press event. Use with getTN().getProperty(path.split('/')[2] + '/propertyId') to get a specific row value.

documents.t: Client-side validation in Klobase operates at two levels: (1) field-level required constraints using the 'required' property, and (2) full-form OnValidate triggered by commitP or saveTransaction. Both are enforced in the browser before any network call is made. D.1 — Required Field Validation​ Mark a control as required by adding the 'required' property and setting it to true. The platform renders a red asterisk and prevents submission if the field is empty. # Action Detail 1 Select the input control Page Builder → select the mandatory field control, e.g. complaint_desc m.Input. 2 Add 'required' property Properties tab → Add → required → set Value to true. 3 Test in Full Preview (CREATE mode) Click New → leave complaint_desc empty → click Save. Platform shows required validation error and blocks save. D.2 — OnValidate (Server-Side Validation Triggered from Client)​ OnValidate runs in the entity file (.ts) on the Private Node when saveTransaction is called with validate=true. The client sends the dirty object to the server; the server validates and returns errors if any rule fails. The client then displays these errors as message dialogs. // In d_complaints.ts entity file — OnValidate hook public async OnValidate(oEvent: IKloEvent): Promise<void> { const entity = oEvent.getEntity(); const errors: string[] = []; // V001: Description must be at least 20 characters if (!entity.complaint_desc || entity.complaint_desc.length < 20) { errors.push('V001: Complaint description must be at least 20 characters.'); } // V002: Priority is mandatory if (!entity.priority) { errors.push('V002: Priority is mandatory.'); } // V003: Cannot close without a remark if (entity.s_status === 'CLOSED' && !entity.remark) { errors.push('V003: Remark is required when closing a complaint.'); } if (errors.length > 0) { oEvent.setError(errors.join('\\n')); } } For OnValidate to fire from the UI, the detail TransNode's setActiveIf must be set to 'Valid' in the Page Data Model. Without this, saveTransaction with validate=true does nothing. # Action Detail 1 Set setActiveIf on detail TransNode Page Data Model → click detail TransNode → setActiveIf dropdown → select Valid. 2 Call saveTransaction with validate=true Edit button press: this.setMode('EDIT'). Save button press: this.saveTransaction('Saved.', 'Save failed.', true, true). 3 Test validation Leave complaint_desc with fewer than 20 characters → Save → OnValidate fires → error message dialog shows V001 text. 4 Fix and retry Enter a valid description → Save → passes validation → data persists → mode resets to DISPLAY.

These standards are non-negotiable on all Procify projects. Violations result in code review rejection and technical debt. The principles come from kloTouch 7.0 Basic Training Guide §7.4 and §7.5. E.1 — Controller File Standards​ Rule Do Don't Reason Scope Write ONLY UI logic in the controller: formatters, navigation, show/hide, model reads for display. Write business logic (status transitions, validations, default-setting) in the controller. Business logic in the controller bypasses server validation and breaks when the screen is accessed via API. TypeScript typing Declare every variable with its type: const count: number = 0; const msg: string = ''; Use implicit any: let x = someValue; or omit types on function parameters. Untyped code hides bugs at compile time that surface as runtime errors in production. Variable declaration Declare variables only when necessary. Prefer const over let. Declare variables at file scope (class properties) when a local variable suffices. File-scope variables persist across page navigations and cause state leakage between sessions. Nested functions Keep functions flat. Extract complex logic to named private methods. Nest arrow functions inside controller methods: onClick(() => { const x = () => {...}; }) Nested functions are not testable, not readable, and difficult to debug. Async/await Use async/await for all TransNode API calls. Mark the function async. Use .then().catch() promise chains. Consistent await pattern is required by the framework for proper error propagation. Deprecated APIs Always use navTo(), tm.commitP(), this.setMode(). Use navToS(), navToByEvent(), getTN('x').commitP() Deprecated APIs are removed in future versions. Using them creates upgrade risk. Model mutation Only modify model properties via setProperty() for transient display values. Directly mutate entity properties from the controller (entity.some_prop = value). Direct mutations bypass the dirty-tracking mechanism and do not persist on save. E.2 — Entity File Standards​ Rule Do Don't Scope Write ONLY business logic in entity files: onCreate defaults, onUpdate role checks, onDelete restrictions, beforeQ filtering, OnValidate. Write navigation or UI state changes in entity files. Setter functions Use setter override pattern to automatically derive related values when a property changes. Compute derived values in the controller on button press — this is bypassed when data changes via API. Validation location All mandatory field checks and business rule violations go in OnValidate. Throw errors in onAfterCreate — onAfterCreate is called AFTER the record is saved; errors there cause data inconsistency. Error handling Always wrap async BOL API calls (createEntityP, LoadEntityByKeyP) in try/catch and log errors. Let unhandled promise rejections propagate silently. Role checks in rules Use oEvent.getTxn().$SYSTEM.roleID to get the runtime role and enforce role-specific logic. Hardcode user IDs or email addresses for role checks. E.3 — Naming Conventions​ Item Convention Example Pages p_ prefix + snake_case description p_complaints, p_complaint_dashboard Page Areas pa_ prefix pa_complaint_details, pa_complaints Sections s_ prefix s_complaints, s_detail_header Entities d_ prefix d_complaints, d_complaint_item Queries q_ prefix q_complaints, q_customers Transient properties t_ prefix t_open_count, t_selected_count Controller functions (formatters) format + PascalCase formatPriority, formatTAT, formatStatusLabel Controller functions (event handlers) on + PascalCase + action onEditPress, onSavePress, onDeleteConfirm Variables in TypeScript camelCase + explicit type const openCount: number = 0; Boolean variables is/has prefix isEscalated, hasAttachment, isLoading ⚠ Private Node must be running whenever you test controller functions, formatter functions, or OnValidate. Without the Private Node, server-side hooks are bypassed and the client shows incorrect results. Always verify Private Node status in the Dev Tools toolbar before testing.

Concept What It Does Where Controller TypeScript UI orchestration only: formatters, model reads/writes for display, dashboard counts. workspace/apps/<app>/p_complaints.controller.ts TransNode setProperty() Updates a model property — triggers UI re-render immediately. Controller function body Vienable — Role Visibility by role ID: EMPLOYEE, EMPLOYEE_MANAGER, IT_TEAM. Vienable Dashboard → Role column Vienable — Status Group Visibility by status group: OPEN, INPROCESS, ACCEPTED, COMPLETED. Vienable Dashboard → Status Group column Vienable — Page Mode Visibility by DISPLAY/EDIT/CREATE. Vienable Dashboard → Page Mode columns $SYSTEM.roleID Runtime role ID of the logged-in user. Used in Entity/Query Rules for role checks. oEvent.getTxn().$SYSTEM.roleID in rules onPageEnter Controller hook fires after page data loads. Use for dashboard count calculations. p_complaint_dashboard.controller.ts

documents.t: ⚠ Complete ALL mandatory tasks before Session 8 Session 8 finalises the menu, home page, versioning, and publishing — the application must be fully working. Mandatory Tasks​ # Action Detail 1 Verify formatPriority formatter Full Preview: complaint with priority = VERY_HIGH shows '🚨 Very High — Immediate Action'. All 4 priority values formatted correctly. 2 Verify Vienable — Edit button CLOSED complaint (COMPLETED group): Edit button absent. OPEN complaint (DISPLAY mode): Edit visible → click → disappears. 3 Verify complaint_desc by role emp_<prid>: OPEN complaint → Edit → complaint_desc editable. INPROCESS complaint → Edit → complaint_desc is Show As Label. mgr_<prid>: always Show As Label. 4 Verify responsible_team by role emp_<prid> in EDIT mode: responsible_team is Show As Label (cannot assign). mgr_<prid> in EDIT mode: responsible_team is editable. 5 Verify dashboard counts p_complaint_dashboard shows live counts. Create/close complaints and reload — counts update correctly. 6 Verify screen size Vienable Page Builder Preview In → Phone: grid shows only ticket_id, priority, s_status. Desktop: all columns visible. | Session 8— App Management, Versioning & Publishing Duration: Full day | Pre-requisite: Session 8 assignment verified | | :---- |

Session Objectives​ By the end of this session, you will be able to: # Objective 1 Create the application menu using the Menu Editor — matching the BRD menu structure exactly. 2 Configure the HomePage Editor to add screen tiles for all three personas. 3 Understand the App Status Lifecycle: ACTIVE → RELEASED → DEPRECATED, and when to transition. 4 Create an App Branch from an RELEASED version and understand the branch-to-version merge workflow. 5 Run Validate & Publish — identify and fix blockers before triggering a Full Build. 6 Transport the published application from DEV to QA using the Transport tool. 7 Perform an end-to-end smoke test covering all three personas (Employee, Manager, IT Team). ⚠ Important Pre-requisite Check — Trainer will verify ALL of these before Session 8 begins. ✔ p_complaints page is fully built: search, list, detail with all tabs populated. ✔ Status badges (OPEN/INPROCESS/etc.) are rendered with correct colours. ✔ Vienable is configured: Edit/Save/Cancel button visibility by Role, Mode, and Status Group. ✔ Dashboard (p_complaint_dashboard) is set as Landing Page for all three roles. ✔ formatPriority formatter renders priority with emoji labels. ✔ OnValidate blocks V001–V005 violations correctly. ✔ All three test users (emp_<prid>, mgr_<prid>, it_<prid>) can log in and see the application. If any item above is incomplete, resolve it BEFORE starting Session 8. 📘 Reference / Tip BRD Quick Reference for Session 8 (from Session 1 Part A) Menu structure: ONE item — 'Complaints' → p_complaints Icon: sap-icon://customer-and-contacts Roles: ALL Pages defined in BRD: p_home_page (home screen tiles) and p_complaints (main screen). p_complaint_dashboard = Landing Page (Session 5) — auto-loads on login. Does NOT need a menu entry. App ID format: customer_complaints_<your_prid> e.g. customer_complaints_pr0045

documents.t: A.1 — What Is the Menu Editor?​ The Menu Editor (also called Menu Builder per PROC-26419) is the tool you use to define the navigation structure visible to users in the hamburger menu of the application at runtime. Without a menu entry, users cannot navigate between screens — they would need to know URLs manually. Access path: Running app → Hamburger menu (☰) → Dev Tools → Menu Editor. A.2 — Menu Fields Reference​ Field Description Rules / Notes Menu ID Unique identifier for this menu item. ONLY alphanumeric + underscores. NO hyphens ( - ). NO spaces. Case-sensitive. Wrong: mn-complaints. Correct: mn_complaints. Target Page Page ID the menu item navigates to. Use the Value Help (VH) icon to pick from existing pages. Do NOT type the page ID manually. Menu Text Label shown to the user in the hamburger menu. Keep it short. Title case. Localisation supported. Page Parameters Optional JSON for navTo params (SS, QP, D, Mode). Leave blank for simple page nav. Not needed for the Complaints entry. Menu Icon SAP icon URI displayed alongside the text. Format: sap-icon://<icon-name>. Must be a valid SAP UI5 icon name. Example: sap-icon://customer-and-contacts. Sequence Sort order in the menu. Lower number = appears first. Use multiples of 10 (10, 20, 30) to leave room for future items. Roles Restrict visibility to specific application roles. Leave BLANK = visible to ALL roles. Fill role IDs (comma-separated) to restrict. Test Navigation Validates the menu item navigates correctly. Always click Test Navigation before saving — catches target page errors early. A.3 — BRD Menu Structure to Implement​ Menu Field Value Menu ID mn_complaints Target Page p_complaints (select from VH) Menu Text Complaints Menu Icon sap-icon://customer-and-contacts Sequence 10 Roles Leave blank — visible to ALL roles (Employee, Manager, IT Team) Page Parameters Not required — leave blank A.4 — Step-by-Step: Creating the Application Menu​ 1 Open Menu Editor In the running application, open the hamburger menu (☰ top-left). Go to Dev Tools → Menu Editor. 2 Select the Application In the App dropdown at the top of the Menu Editor, select customer_complaints_<prid>. Click the Edit button (pencil icon ✏). The menu table becomes editable. 3 Add a Header Group Click Add (+) → Add Header. Fill in: Menu ID: hdr_main Menu Text: Main Sequence: 10 Roles: leave blank Click OK. (A Header groups child items visually in the menu.) 4 Add the Complaints Child Menu Item Select the hdr_main row in the table. Click Add (+) → Add Child. Fill in: Menu ID: mn_complaints Target Page: p_complaints (use VH picker) Menu Text: Complaints Menu Icon: sap-icon://customer-and-contacts Sequence: 10 Roles: leave blank Click OK. 5 Test the Navigation Click Test Navigation on the mn_complaints row. p_complaints should open correctly. If a 'Page not found' error appears — check that the Target Page is exactly p_complaints (no typos). 6 Save Click the Save button (disk icon 💾). Wait for the busy dialog to close. A success toast confirms the menu is saved. 7 Verify with All Personas Log out and log in separately as emp_<prid>, mgr_<prid>, and it_<prid>. In each session, open the hamburger menu. The 'Complaints' item must be visible and navigate to p_complaints for ALL three test users. ⚠ Important Common Menu Editor Mistakes Hyphen in Menu ID: mn-complaints causes the item to save but NEVER appear in the app. Always use underscore: mn_complaints. Typing Target Page manually: Always use the VH picker. Manual typos cause silent navigation failures. Saving without testing: Always click 'Test Navigation' before saving. It catches missing pages early. Role restriction accident: If the menu item is set to a specific role, other personas cannot see it. Leave Roles blank for all-role visibility.

B.1 — What Is the HomePage Editor?​ The HomePage Editor configures which screen tiles appear on the application's built-in Home grid — accessible via the Home (🏠) icon. This is separate from the Landing Page (p_complaint_dashboard configured in Session 5). The Landing Page loads automatically on login. The Home grid gives users tile-based navigation to frequently used screens. 📘 Reference / Tip Three 'home' concepts — don't confuse them Landing Page (Session 5): Configured via Landing Page Settings. Auto-loads after login. Shows p_complaint_dashboard. HomePage Editor: Tile grid shown when user clicks the Home (🏠) icon. Configure p_complaints and p_complaint_dashboard tiles here. p_home_page (BRD): A screen defined in the BRD. Can be built as an additional home screen — not required for this session's delivery. B.2 — HomePage Editor Fields Reference​ Field Description HomePageID Unique ID for this tile. Convention: hp_<screen_short_name>. Screen The Page ID this tile navigates to. Use VH to select. Position Where the tile appears on the home grid. Use 'Body' for standard tiles. Sequence Order of the tile. Lower = appears first. Role Restrict tile visibility to specific roles. Leave blank = all roles. B.3 — Step-by-Step: Adding Tiles to HomePage Editor​ 1 Open HomePage Editor Hamburger menu (☰) → Dev Tools → HomePage Editor. Select customer_complaints_<prid> from the App dropdown. Click the Edit icon (✏). 2 Add the Dashboard Tile Click Add (+). HomePageID: hp_dashboard Screen: p_complaint_dashboard (select via VH) Position: Body Sequence: 5 Role: leave blank (all roles) Click Save (do NOT navigate away yet). 3 Add the Complaints Tile Click Add (+). HomePageID: hp_all_complaints Screen: p_complaints (select via VH) Position: Body Sequence: 10 Role: leave blank (all roles) Click Save. 4 Save All Click the Save icon (💾) in the toolbar. Wait for busy dialog to close. Success toast confirms. 5 Verify Log out. Log in as emp_<prid>. Click the Home (🏠) icon. Two tiles must appear: 'Dashboard' and 'Complaints'. Click each tile — verify it navigates to the correct screen. Repeat with mgr_<prid> and it_<prid>.

C.1 — App Status Values​ Every version of an application on the Procify platform has a Status that controls what operations are allowed on it. Understanding these statuses is essential before releasing or transporting. Status Meaning Can Develop? Can Transport? Can Create New Version? ACTIVE Current working version. All development happens here. ✅ Yes ❌ No ❌ No RELEASED Development complete and locked. Ready for transport. ❌ No ✅ Yes ✅ Yes (create from RELEASED) DEPRECATED Retired. Superseded by a newer version. ❌ No ❌ No ❌ No DISCARDED Abandoned branch/version. Excluded from main path. ❌ No ❌ No ❌ No ⚠ Important Critical Versioning Rules — memorise these before proceeding A NEW VERSION can only be created from a RELEASED version. A BRANCH can only be created from an ACTIVE version. Branch flavors CANNOT be transported. Merge the branch into a new version first, then transport. Once status is changed to RELEASED, no further development is possible on that version. Always build (Validate & Publish) BEFORE changing status to RELEASED. C.2 — Step-by-Step: Releasing the Application​ 1 Navigate to Account Console (also called Workspace Hub) Open the hamburger menu → Sys Admin → Account Console (or Workspace Hub). Alternatively: Hamburger menu → My Apps (if visible in your role). 2 Find Your Application In the Apps list, search for customer_complaints_<prid>. Click the App ID to open the application detail screen. 3 Open Edit Mode Click the Edit button (pencil icon ✏) in the toolbar. The Status field becomes editable. 4 Change Status to RELEASED In the Status dropdown, select RELEASED. Read the confirmation message carefully — this action locks all development on this version. Click Save. The app status changes to RELEASED. The Edit icon in Data Studio and Page Builder will now be disabled for this version. 5 Verify In the App detail, the Status badge shows RELEASED. Open Data Studio → select customer_complaints_<prid> → click the Edit icon. You should see a message that the app is locked for editing.
documents.s: Part C — App Status Lifecycle & Versioning

documents.t: D.1 — Why Branch?​ A Branch creates a parallel ACTIVE copy of your application. Use it when you need to work on next-phase enhancements while the current version is being tested in QA. The branch is fully isolated — changes in the branch don't affect the main RELEASED version until you explicitly merge them. Scenario Use Branch? Bug fix on the current version in QA ❌ No — fix directly in main, create new minor version New feature development while current is in QA ✅ Yes — branch from current ACTIVE version Experimental UI changes for client review ✅ Yes — branch lets you show without committing to main D.2 — Step-by-Step: Creating a Branch​ 1 Go to Account Console → My Apps Locate customer_complaints_<prid>. The app must be in ACTIVE status to create a branch. 2 Click Branch In the app detail view, click the Branch button (visible only when status = ACTIVE). The platform creates a new Branch Flavor automatically. The branch version appears in the My Apps list with a branch indicator. 3 Assign Users to the Branch Click the branch version to open its detail. Go to the Roles & Users tab → click Edit. Assign ALL three test users and your developer account to their respective roles. ⚠ Users are NOT copied automatically from the parent — you must assign them manually in the branch. 4 Develop in the Branch Open Data Studio or Page Builder. In the App dropdown, select the BRANCH version (not the main version). Make your changes. Save and test independently. D.3 — Branch Merge Workflow (Summary)​ When the branch is ready to be merged back into the main release cycle: 1 Export Both ZIPs Account Console → Export section. Download ZIP of the main RELEASED version (Set 1) and the branch version (Set 2). 2 Open App Compare & Merge Account Console → App Compare & Merge. Upload Set 1 (main) as Left and Set 2 (branch) as Right. Click Compare. 3 Review the Differences The tool lists differences per component: entities, pages, queries, VH, menus, etc. For each difference, select which version to keep: Set 1 (main), Set 2 (branch), or a Custom combination. 4 Download Merged ZIP Once all decisions are made, click Download to export the merged ZIP. 5 Create New Version and Import In Account Console, create a new Major or Minor version from the current RELEASED main version. Import the merged ZIP into the new version. Run Update Schema, Full Build, and test before releasing. 📘 Reference / Tip Reference: App Branching & Merging User Guide — App_Branching___Merging-User_Guide.docx PROC-26419 note: 'Account Console' may be renamed 'Workspace Hub' in platform help content. Both names refer to the same tool.

documents.t: E.1 — Validate vs. Publish — What's the Difference?​ Action What It Does When to Use Validate Scans the application for errors WITHOUT building. Safe — nothing changes in the running app. Run first, every time. Fix all errors before triggering Publish. Publish Validates first, then builds the app if no blocking errors exist. Updates the running app. After Validate passes with 0 errors. Use Full Build for first publish or after VH Config changes. E.2 — Common Publish Blockers​ Blocker Cause Fix VH Config not visible in UI after Publish VH Config changes require a Full Build. Always select 'Full Build' for the first publish or after adding/editing VH Configs. TypeScript compilation error Syntax error in entity .ts or controller .ts file. Open VS Code → check terminal for tsc errors → fix, save, re-validate. Update Schema not run Entity properties added but schema not updated in DB. Data Studio → select entity → Update Schema → confirm success toast. Another build IN-QUEUE A previous build is already running. Click 'Proceed' to queue behind the current build. Do NOT cancel it. Missing app_util flavor Validate and Publish menu not visible. Ask trainer — app_util must be assigned to your developer account. E.3 — Step-by-Step: Validate and Publish​ 1 Open Validate and Publish Hamburger menu (☰) → Dev Tools → Validate and Publish. (If this menu item is missing, app_util flavor is not assigned to your account. Ask the trainer.) 2 Enter the Application In the App field, type customer_complaints_<prid> and press Enter. The application version details load. 3 Run Validate First Select Action: Validate. Click Submit. Wait for the validation report to generate. Download the XLSX report if errors are listed. Fix every ERROR before proceeding. Warnings can be reviewed but do not block the build. 4 Fix All Errors For each error in the report: - Missing Update Schema → Data Studio → Update Schema on the entity. - TypeScript error → VS Code → fix tsc error → save → re-validate. - Missing VH Build → select Full Build in the next step. Re-run Validate until the report shows 0 errors. 5 Run Publish Select Action: Publish. Build Type: Full Build (required for first publish and after any VH Config changes). Click Submit. The Publish Log shows the progression: IN-QUEUE → IN-PROCESS → PUBLISHED Do NOT navigate away while the build is running. 6 Verify the Published App Log out completely. Log back in. Open the hamburger menu → confirm 'Complaints' item is visible. Navigate to p_complaints → confirm live data loads. Verify: status badges render, VH dropdowns populate, all tabs in detail section work. 📘 Reference / Tip Publish Logs reference: Publish_Logs_Screen.docx — explains each status stage and error codes. Validate & Publish reference: Publish_or_Validate_Screen-7_0_App_utility__.docx

F.1 — How Transport Works​ Transport is a PULL mechanism: the TARGET system (QA) asks the SOURCE system (DEV) for the latest published version. You perform ALL transport steps while logged into the QA environment, not DEV. Stage What Happens Setup Transport creates entries in QA metadata tables for the application, groups, and flavors. Download Application ZIPs are pulled from DEV and extracted in the QA server's file system. Update Schema Database tables for all entities are created or altered in the QA database. Finalising Application is set to ACTIVE in QA so users can log in and access it. ⚠ Important Transport Pre-requisites — verify ALL before starting 1. The application must be in RELEASED status on the DEV system. 2. Branch flavors CANNOT be transported. Create a new version, merge, then transport. 3. The QA server's config.json must have mm_klo_online_server pointing to the DEV landscape URL. 4. A host file entry for the DEV system must exist on the QA server. 5. The transport_1 app must be assigned to the developer account on the QA system. If any pre-requisite is missing, the transport will fail at Setup or Download stage. Ask the trainer to verify the QA environment config before proceeding. F.2 — Step-by-Step: Transporting to QA​ 1 Log in to the QA System Open the QA environment URL in a browser (trainer provides the URL). Log in with your developer credentials. ⚠ ALL remaining steps are done on QA, not on DEV. 2 Navigate to App Transport Hamburger menu (☰) → Sys Admin → App Transport. The App Transport screen lists all available applications from the connected DEV system. 3 Find Your Application In the list, locate customer_complaints_<prid>. If not visible, toggle the 'Show All' button to see all available apps (not just those with pending updates). 4 Click the App Row Click on customer_complaints_<prid>. A detail panel opens showing available versions from DEV and any already-installed versions in QA. 5 Install As Writable Click the available version update. A dialog appears with two options: As Readable — locked, cannot edit in QA. As Writable — editable, allows continued development in QA. Click 'As Writable' (recommended for training so you can fix issues in QA if needed). 6 Accept Conditions and Proceed A mandatory conditions dialog appears. For each mandatory item (⚠ icon), tick the acceptance checkbox. If prompted about shared flavor movement (on QA/PROD systems), click Proceed. Click Proceed to start the transport. 7 Monitor Transport Stages The screen shows progress through: Setup → Download → Update Schema → Finalising. Wait for each stage to complete. The overall status changes to ACTIVE when done. 8 Assign Users in QA After transport, the app is ACTIVE in QA but has NO users assigned. Go to Account Console → My Apps → customer_complaints_<prid>. Go to Roles & Users tab → assign: emp_<prid> → Employee role mgr_<prid> → Manager role it_<prid> → ResponsibleTeam role Your developer account → Manager role 9 Verify in QA Log out of the QA developer session. Log in as emp_<prid> in QA. Verify: hamburger menu shows 'Complaints', p_complaints loads, all VH dropdowns work. Repeat with mgr_<prid> and it_<prid>. 📘 Reference / Tip Transport User Guide: Transport-_User_Guide.docx The Transport tool supports DEV → QA, QA → PROD, and DEV → DEV movement. Script Master (second tab in Transport screen) shows automated scripts maintained for the system — ask trainer if any scripts need to be run after transport.

documents.t: This smoke test must be completed AFTER publish. It verifies every major feature built across all 8 sessions works correctly in the published application. Run it on DEV first, then repeat on QA after transport. # Persona Action Expected Result 1 EMPLOYEE (emp_<prid>) Login → Menu → Complaints. Click Add (with Object Type = PROCIFY). Fill complaint_desc (10+ chars), priority = HIGH, select customer from picker. Click Save. complaint_id = P-000XX auto-generated. s_status = OPEN. assigned_to = emp_<prid>. Record appears in list. 2 EMPLOYEE Open the new complaint → Edit → Clear complaint_desc → Save. V001 error blocks save: 'Complaint description must be at least 10 characters'. 3 EMPLOYEE Edit → priority dropdown. ComboBox shows Low / Medium / High / Critical (from vhc_priority). 4 EMPLOYEE Edit → customer_id field. F4 picker opens showing d_customers records. 5 MANAGER (mgr_<prid>) Login → open the OPEN complaint → Edit → set responsible_team from picker → Save. responsible_team field is editable for Manager. Record saves. Status remains OPEN. 6 IT TEAM (it_<prid>) Login → open assigned complaint → Edit → s_status = INPROCESS → Save. Status badge changes to INPROCESS (orange colour). Edit button remains visible. 7 EMPLOYEE Open INPROCESS complaint → Edit → try s_status = CLOSED → Save. V005 error: 'Employees cannot close a complaint'. 8 MANAGER Open INPROCESS complaint → Edit → s_status = CLOSED → closed_on = today → Save. Status badge changes to CLOSED (grey). Edit button disappears (COMPLETED Vienable). actual_tat computed in Data Browser. 9 ALL ROLES Navigate to Home (🏠). Two tiles visible: Dashboard and Complaints. Each tile navigates correctly. 10 ALL ROLES Preview In → Phone (Page Builder). Grid in s_complaints shows only 3 columns (ticket_id, priority, s_status) on phone view.

All three personas (Employee, Manager, IT Team) have correct access, menu, and data visibility. After this assignment you will have built and shipped a complete enterprise application from scratch. Log on to the test system. (Get all the credentials from the Admin Team) User: Use your User ID (PRID) Password: Use your password. The Procify Data Studio app will be assigned to you.

Data that are stored in the database are in table format. Procify Data Studio is used to create tables for our database. In BOL, all entities and queries act as attributes of the table. 1.0.1 The Editor is divided into two major sections: Tree Detail
The app or Flavor selection drop-down contains a list of apps that have been assigned to the user. By using the drop down users can select the app on which users are going to work on.
Once the app is selected, it will list down all the entities present inside the selected app. To select any specific entity, click on that entity.
You can search for any entity by filling in the entity name in the search field provided in the entity list section.

Procify Data Studio supports two types of modes, Normal mode and Expert mode. Normal Mode - It supports all the basic functionalities like Entity, Query, and Value Help creation along with app settings. Expert Mode - It supports all the functionalities from the normal mode along with add-on features like Status Config, config properties for object type, and entity indexes. Note: One can switch between the two modes at any point in time.
Create button lists down various options for table creation. Create Menu supports the below actions: Entity Entity From Template Query Value Help

By default, the editor will be in non-editable mode. Clicking on the edit button will make the data editable. Once the edit mode is enabled, it will update the list of available options in the toolbar. The mode gets changed to editable and the save option will be enabled. The below icon shows the save icon which will be used for committing the changes to the DB.

Once the entity is in editable mode, it lists down the list of available options as shown in the below image. 1.7.1. Update Schema​ Once all the metadata regarding the entity is provided and saved, the update schema is used to convert the entity into an actual database table. 1.7.2. Delete​ This option will be used for deleting any item selected in the left tree. Using this option, any item like entity/query or value help can be deleted. 1.7.3. Validate​ The validate option verifies whether the metadata maintained for the entity is correct or not. 1.7.4. Read Only​ The read-only and cancel options are only visible in editable mode. On the click of the read-only icon, the editor becomes non-editable. 1.7.5. MetaData File​ This comprises the metadata file that you want to upload from your local system to the Procify Data Studio. 1.7.6 Test​ Test allows checking the CRUD operation on the created/selected which stands for create, read, update, and delete. These are four basic functions executed in relational database applications. 1.7.7. Import from SAP​ This option imports the selected entity & its properties from SAP tables. Developers can import an entity -> verify their changes -> and then click “Save” to commit their changes. Pre-requisite: In config.json, under “mm_klobroker_ext” array, an object needs to be maintained having details as follow, mentioning the connection between your flavor in platform and the respective SAP system: The flavor should have some entities already maintained in SAP-side which will be used to import. Steps: Navigate to “Design Studio” -> “Procify Data Studio” Screen and select your flavor. The flavor needs to be configured on the SAP side. The flavor_name and major_version should be the same. The minor version and patch version can be different from each other. Create a new entity and do not add any properties yet. Otherwise, use an existing entity having some existing properties. And then click the “Import from SAP” button. If the entity is maintained in the SAP-side, then it will show an error dialog. Else, the import process will start. Validation: During the process, if any error comes it will throw the error dialog. And in case any validation fails e.g., propertyid values are having reserved keywords then it will show that respective dialog also - same validation as available we developer normally create properties from the screen. List of reserved keywords: PROC-27544: List of Reserved Keywords in Data Studio Application. Once the import process starts, at the end step, it will ask the developer to skip any specific properties by selecting the checkbox and clicking the “Skip” button or click “Sync All” to accept all data from the payload. Important: Import from SAP on Existing Entity After import is done, developers can save more properties and save it. Note: SAP Import process only imports the entity and properties. After import, the developer needs to click the Save button to commit all changes. 1.7.7.1. Import from SAP on Existing Entity Data​ While doing import again on an existing entity having existing properties, it will ask the developer regarding the existing properties whether to keep those properties or delete them. For example, here my_key_1 is a property not present in the sap table and is an existing property in the Procify-side table. So, here, if the developer will mark the checkbox of it and click “Skip”, then it will not delete that property. If the developer clicks “Sync All”, then it will delete the existing properties and import only SAP-side, non-skipped properties. 1.7.8. Import from SAP Child​ This option imports the children entity(s) from an existing parent entity from SAP tables. Does not include relations. Developers can import an entity -> verify their changes -> and then click “Save” to commit their changes. Pre-requisite is the same as mentioned in the Import from SAP section. Steps: Validation: If a developer has created a parent entity and triggered “Import from SAP Child” before saving the parent entity, then it will throw a validation error. So, it is needed to create & save its parent entity first, before importing its respective children entities. If the parent entity is maintained in the SAP-side, then it will show an error dialog. Else, the import process will start. From Procify Data Studio, select the flavor -> click the parent entity -> click edit button -> click “Import from SAP Child“ button. Validation: During the process, if any error comes it will throw the error dialog. And in case any validation fails e.g., propertyid values are having reserved keywords then it will show that respective dialog also - same validation as available we developer normally create properties from the screen. List of reserved keywords: PROC-27544: List of Reserved Keywords in Data Studio Application. Once the import process starts, at the end step, it will ask the developer to skip any specific properties by selecting the checkbox and clicking the “Skip” button or click “Sync All” to accept all data from the payload. Important: Import from SAP Child on Existing Entity Important: Before Save, developers need to maintain the Primary Keys in all of the imported children entities. Otherwise, it will throw a validation error before clicking Save. After maintaining the Primary Keys in all imported children entities, it will allow the developers to save the changes. Important: As relations are not maintained via the import process, after save, developers need to maintain the relations manually from the Procify Data Studio tool. Parent to Child Primary Relation: Child to Grandchild Primary Relation: Once the relations are maintained, the developers can start using the entity’s data browser or from screen for CRUD operations. 1.7.8.1. Import from SAP Child on Existing Entity Data​ Mentioned in 1.7.7.1 .
Procify Data Studio is divided into two major sections, which are listed below: Tree Detail

The tree present in the left section lists all the entities present in the selected app. 2.1.1. Expand All​ Expand All option is to expand all the collapsed sections (entity, query, value help). 2.1.2 Collapse All​ Collapse all option is to collapse all the expanded sections (entity, query, value help)

This section contains all the details related to the selected entity/query or value help like properties, relations, object type, status, queries, and many more. 2.2.1 Entity Detail​ On selection of any entity in the tree, it will display all available options in the detail section. The description of each tab is given below: 2.2.1.1. Detail​ This section contains all the basic information about the entity. It contains fields like Root Entity name, App Mode, Entity Icon, Entity Name, Metadata type, and also a few buttons to enable or disable CRUD over the entity. The description of each field is provided below: BO/Root Entity :​ BO stands for Business Object. Root Entity means that if any entity is a root entity then it will have the same name as the BO and it will be the parent entity. App Mode :​ App mode refers to the network mode of the entity/query. It supports network modes such as those specified below: Offline :​ Offline network mode refers to the capability to run the program with weak or infrequent network availability. The application stores the relevant data locally and updates the local cache and server data as and when it finds connectivity. Browsers and installed mobile apps (client) both are capable of offline operations. In offline mode, the values are maintained/fetched from the web SQL. Online :​ Online network mode refers to the capability of running the program in a browser or installed mobile app (client) to communicate with the server for day-to-day needs. Network connectivity from client to server is a must. All the changes on the browser or device app will be collected and sent to the server for validating and saving. In the online mode, the values are maintained/fetched from the transactional database. SAP Online :​ This refers to the capability of all the transactions that go to SAP via the gateway server. In SAP online mode the values are maintained/fetched from the SAP server. SAP Preferred Online :​ Any transaction that takes place between your application goes through SAP to your web SQL. Entity Icon :​ This will associate the specified icon with the entity. Entity Name :​ Entity name refers to the actual name/id of the entity. Metadata type:​ Runtime entity: This is the default type of entity, where the table persists in the DB (unlike Transient Entities). The table is created in the Trans DB and CRUD operations can be performed on it. Config entity: This is the type of entity, where the table persists but only in meta DB. This is usually used to store data for status and role fields. **Transient Entities:**A transient entity is a non-persistent entity—meaning it does not store data in the database. It is primarily used for runtime calculations, data aggregation, or displaying derived data in the UI. These entities are ideal when you need to display or process combined data from multiple sources without storing it permanently. {#transient-entities:a-transient-entity-is-a-non-persistent-entity—meaning-it-does-not-store-data-in-the-database.-it-is-primarily-used-for-runtime-calculations,-data-aggregation,-or-displaying-derived-data-in-the-ui.-these-entities-are-ideal-when-you-need-to-display-or-process-combined-data-from-multiple-sources-without-storing-it-permanently.}​ Use Case Example: Suppose you have two entities and want to display certain fields from each, but do not wish to persist the combined data. In this case: Create a transient entity that includes only the required properties. Write custom logic to query both source entities. Populate the transient entity with the result. Display this transient data on the screen with full support for UI features like Sort, Filter, and Fuzzy Search. Users can also fetch data from external sources, populate the transient entity, and leverage built-in platform features such as:Sort, Filter, Fuzzy search, Excel download,Pivot view (report/chart generation). NOTE: Data Must Be Fully Loaded:The transient entity’s query must execute with loadAll: true. Unique Primary Key: Ensure that the transient entity has a unique primary key to enable proper identification and UI support. Custom Data Handling Logic: You must define how and from where the data is fetched, processed, and whether or not it should be saved back to a persistent entity. Persists On :​ Persists On consists of three options which are explained below: null -​ Entities will be created based on the app’s network mode. If the network mode of the app is online then it will be created on the server side. If the network mode of the app is offline then it will be created in web sql. Both -​ Entities will be created for both sides. Client Only -​ An entity will only be created in web SQL for the device or browser during registration. Server Only -​ An entity will be created in server-side DB and not in web SQL. NOTE: Entity persistence will be decided primarily based on the Persists On mentioned. In case the persist on is set as null , Persists On will be checked based on app network mode. Offline Flavor - Entity will be created in both server and client DB Online Flavor - Entity will be created only on server DB. Universal Link Details :​ Universal Link Details is used to build a Universal Link that opens the specific record of the current entity in its respective screen based on the provided parameters. These parameters are similar to navTo parameters available in screens which will be used for generating the deep link. Target Page -​ Screen Id of the page. Section -​ Section to which the link needs to be navigated. Page Data Model -​ Name of the transnode to which the link needs to be navigated. Query Parameters -​ Additional QueryParameters that need to be passed to the navigated screen. Create Allowed:​ This button enables/disables the creation accessibility over the entity. Read Allowed:​ This button enables/disables the data read access over the entity. Delete Allowed:​ This button enables/disables the deletion accessibility over the entity. Update Allowed:​ This button enables/disables the modification access over the entity. 2.2.1.2. Properties​ This tab contains all the properties present inside the entity. It is also used to add/delete properties from the entity. Entity Property is also known as an attribute or variable in an entity or field in the database table. The entity Detail section consists of multiple fields. All the fields are explained below : Entity Property ID :​ Property ID is unique within the entity across all apps. Once created this can’t be changed later. PROC-27544: List of Reserved Keywords in Data Studio Application - List of reserved keywords which are not restricted to use as property ID value. Short Label :​ Provide label for your property which will be used as labels in screen. Note: It is recommended not to provide same label for two or more properties. Validation Warning: Key Attributes :​ Key attributes show whether the property is a primary key, mandatory, or auto-incrementing field. Each of these attributes is explained in the below table: Icon Description This icon shows if the respective property is a primary key or not. If it’s highlighted, then it’s a primary key, else not. Each entity should have a primary key irrespective of the entity type This icon shows whether the selected property is mandatory or not. If any property is marked as compulsory, its value needs to be maintained before saving it to the DB. If the icon is highlighted, the entity is compulsory. This icon represents whether the respective property has auto-incrementing functionality or not. This icon indicates whether the chosen property is a unique key. When highlighted, it means the selected property will only store unique data in the database. If a user attempts to add duplicate data, an error will occur. This icon indicates whether the selected property is a Parent key, meaning it is common to both the parent and child entities. A parent key is created only when a child entity exists, and all primary keys of the parent entity are established as parent keys in the child entity. Value Help :​ Can set the already defined value help for this property. Default Value :​ It refers to the predefined value for that specific property. This field will be automatically filled with the specified value. Qualifier :​ Add a Qualifier for the entity. A qualifier helps to make the entity property work in a predefined manner. The property with qualifier stores and acts as per the definition of the qualifier. Please refer to Qualifiers to know more about qualifiers. Root :​ All primary properties of a Business Object (BO) will be designated as Root keys in its child entities. This can be identified by checking the property details and if the Root checkbox is true,it indicates that the property is a root key. On adding data using a data browser, it will copy the data of the Root Key from its immediate parent.​ NOTE 1: Root keys are created only when the child entity is created. NOTE 2: In the case of the Parent Child flavor scenario, the data type (domain, length, etc.) for the same Property Id in both the flavors should not be the same. Is Unique Key:​ A unique key can be assigned to any property, aside from the primary key. When a child entity is created, all the root and parent keys are automatically marked as unique, and an index is generated for them. Any regular property can be designated as a unique key. Use Case of Unique Key: Consider a student table that includes columns for registration number (reg_no), student name (student_name), and date of birth (date_of_birth), with multiple records where the reg_no is the primary key. reg_no(Primary) student_name date_of_birth 1001 Ankit 21/04/2001 1002 Abhijith 22/08/2005 1003 Amit 12/02/2004 1004 Prem 08/05/2000 Consider adding a new column, “aadhar_no,” to store the Aadhaar numbers of all the students. Since each Aadhaar number should be unique, we want to ensure the database doesn't allow duplicate entries. The only option available is to mark “aadhar_no” as a primary key, but this would prevent the user from making any updates to the existing data. To solve this, the concept of a unique key is introduced. By marking the “aadhar_no” as a unique key, we ensure that duplicate values can't be stored in the column while still allowing null values. This allows us to modify the data in the table without enforcing a primary key constraint. reg_no(Primary) student_name aadhar_no(unique) date_of_birth 1001 Ankit 21/04/2001 1002 Abhijith 22071 22/08/2005 1003 Amit 12/02/2004 1004 Prem 08/05/2000 When a property is marked as unique, it offers the following benefits: It prevents the storage of duplicate data, regardless of case (case-insensitive). It allows null values to be stored in the column. When creating a child entity, it is mandatory to mark a property as unique to support the "one parent, multiple children" concept. This is because the parent key, which is unique, will be fetched from the parent entity and referenced in the child. If someone tries to add another child with the same parent data, a unique key violation will occur. To resolve this, an additional unique key must be defined in the child entity that is independent of the parent entity. When a unique key is defined in a child entity that has a primary relationship with a parent entity, uniqueness is enforced as a composite constraint comprising the parent key and the child unique key (i.e., parent_key + unique_key). Is Parent Key:​ All the primary properties of the immediate parent entity will be created as Parent Key in the child entity and will be marked as regular. This property cannot be changed by the user. On adding data from Data Browser, it will copy the Parent Key data from its parent and create it in the child. Formula:​ It is a property of an entity. It evaluates the given expression and returns the evaluated result. Example : Syntax : ={“test ”+ this.order_id } Here this.order_id is the entity property Data Type:​ It is a property data type. Ex- String, Boolean, Integer.Data type conversion in the Procify Data Studio is only available for compatible data types, as outlined in the provided Excel file;Data Type Conversion. Filter Option:​ If this field is marked as true for a property then only applyFilterP API can be used for that property. Is Restricted:​ If this field is marked as true for a property which has a value help assigned to it then validation will be called for this property in UI which will check if the key is present in the value help. Min Value:​ The minimum value is the minimum value for your property that a user can enter. Max Value:​ The maximum value is the maximum value for your property that a user can enter. Authorization:​ The authorization field takes the Login user id as an input and only that user can get access to that property. Ex- $USER.login_id ID Series : ID series is used for populating the IDs/Keys in the entity’s property with kloBO. If an application wants to allocate the ID itself, either it should not assign the ID series or mark it as none. kloBO will allocate the ID on the first read of the ID. Transient Property:​ An entity property can be made transient by setting the type of property to “Transient Field” so that within that entity property’s value is not stored in the database. It exists only at runtime and is never persisted in or retrieved from the database. Use Cases: Accessing Properties of Relational Entities Transient fields can be used to display values from related entities without actually adding them as properties/database table columns. For example, if an entity is related to another entity(e.g., User → Department), a transient field like departmentName can fetch and show department.name without requiring an actual field in the database. Custom Getter/Setter Logic Standard transient property getters and setters can be used for dynamically calculating values, formatting data before sending it in a response, or temporarily accepting input and storing it without saving it to the database. In this example, d_customer is the entity, and fullName is a transient property. The fullName property is computed from the underlying firstName and lastName fields. The getter and setter for fullName should be written directly inside the entity file /src/<app folder>/entity/d_customer.ts Eg: get fullName(): string { return `${this.firstName} ${this.lastName}`; } set fullName(name: string) { const [firstName, lastName] = name.split(' '); this.firstName = firstName; this.lastName = lastName; } Note : In case a user wants to change the property type of any property, they have to re-add the same property in their screen metadata using Procify Page Builder (wherever applicable) from their transnode for reflecting the changes. For ex: This is the property type created by default using Procify Data Studio: Suppose the property type has been changed as per below: To reflect the same changes in the application as well please follow the mentioned steps: Step 1: Open the screen metadata in the Procify Page Builder. Now delete all occurrences of the changed property type’s property. Step 2: Now drag and drop the same property from the transnode to the section. 2.2.1.3. Relations​ This tab contains all the relations created inside the entity. Entity relation relates one entity with another entity. Entity relation consists of multiple fields. All the fields are explained below: Relation Type:​ It specifies the type of the relation whether it’s a primary or non-primary relation. This also contains two icons which are described below: Primary Relation​ Primary relation is a special kind of aggregate relation within the BO boundary. All entities in a BO are navigable from the root entity only once unidirectional. A primary relation is a direct relation between two entities. There will be a parent entity and a child entity and the child entity will be dependent on the parent entity. The Return Entity value help is applicable only for aggregate (non-primary) relations. The primary relation is created only during the creation of a child entity and cannot be assigned by selecting a return entity. Aggregated Relation​ An aggregation relationship can be described in simple words as "an object of one class can own or access the objects of another class". If a parent is deleted/archived, all other parts associated with it are deleted. Aggregated relations can be across BOs. When a relation is created as non-primary, the related data cannot be fetched in callbacks if both the parent and child entities are being saved in the same transaction. This occurs because the child entity has not yet been persisted at the time the relation is evaluated, and therefore the relation data is unavailable. Icon Description This shows whether a relation is primary or not. This icon displays whether a relation is aggregated or not. Relation Name:​ Unique within an Entity. Relation names and Property names can’t be the same. Description:​ Provides a small description of the relation. Return Entity:​ Return entity is the actual name of the entity. Relation Query:​ The relation Query is the entity/query ID using which the relation needs to be established. NOTE: If the relation is created using a relation query, the relational data will be fetched according to that query. Therefore, features like sort order should be implemented at the query level, rather than at the entity level, to retrieve the data in the correct sorted order. Cardinality:​ Cardinality shows how the entities are connected. Select the cardinality for the relation (0:n, 1:1, 1:n). 0:n - Zero to Many relationships (A minimum cardinality of 0 indicates that the relationship is optional.) 1:1 - One to One relationship 1:n - One to Many relationships Mapping:​ It will map based on the target entity property and source entity property with a mapping type. This field provides the following options: ON CREATE ( mapping will be called On Create of an entity) ON QUERY ( mapping will be called On execution of an entity query) BOTH Note:​ In case of aggregated relation where the mapping property of the entity is null, then all the data of the related entity will be fetched from the relation 2.2.1.4. Object Type​ Object Type defines the possible behaviour of an entity / BO. Object type has a unique key and description. Object type contains multiple fields which are explained below: Object Type:​ This field displays the object type. The object type may include alphabets or numerals. Object Group:​ It is a group of object types. Select the object group from the drop-down. 2.2.1.5. Status​ This tab is used for the configuration and maintenance of status-based data under specified object types. This also helps in assigning status, and status groups under specific object types. This tab consists of a few fields which are mentioned below. Object Type:​ This field displays the object types available for this entity. The object type may include alphabets or numerals. Icon:​ This field displays an icon for your newly created entry in the status section. Description:​ A short description Status:​ This field displays the entity status which you are going to map with the status group Status Group: This field lists down the predefined status groups, which can be mapped with the status and will be used in Vienable. NOTE: If changing any system field property’s (s_status, s_object_type, s_status_group) propertytype columns, will change it in the whole app. For ex: If changing the value help id of s_status property from “vh_s_status” to “vhc_city” then this change will reflect in each of the entities s_status property wherever added. 2.2.1.6. Queries​ This tab will list all the queries present under the current entity. Using this section we can also add new queries. Queries consist of a few fields like Query ID and description. Query ID:​ The query ID is the name of the query which is used to identify the specific query. Description:​ A short description of the query. 2.2.1.7. Entity Index​ The Entity index tab is used to retrieve data from a database very fast. When you are creating indexing, It will create an index in your database along with the properties you have added. Next time when you search those properties, It will directly fetch that index from the database and give you the data. An index on a table works like an index in a book (that's where the name came from): Let's say you have a book about databases and want to find some information about storage. Without an index (assuming no other aid, such as a table of contents) you'd have to go through the pages one by one until you found the topic (that's a full table scan). On the other hand, an index has a list of keywords, so you'd consult the index and see that storage is mentioned on pages 113-120,231 and 354. Then you could flip to those pages directly, without searching (that's a search with an index, somewhat faster). Entity Index creation: Step 1: Go to the Entity Index tab and click on the add icon(+) Entity index consists of a few fields which are mentioned below: ID: The entity index ID is used to identify the specific entity index. Description: A short description of the entity index. Properties: Properties for your indexing. These properties data will be retrieved very fast. Client/Server: Entity indexing will call on which side, server-side, client-side or both. Step 2: Fill in the detail section as per your requirement. Step 3: Click on the save button. NOTE: Indices will be created based on the Client/Server mentioned. Server Only - Creates index only in server DB Client Only - Creates only in client/local DB Both - Creates on both server and client Deletion of Entity Indexes is supported at both entity level and flavor level update schema , but some points have to be kept under consideration. In a parent-child scenario, if an index is deleted from the parent but still exists in the child, triggering an update schema on the child entity will cause the index to be added back. To avoid inconsistencies, an index must be deleted from both the parent and child entities. 2.2.1.8. Rules​ A Rule is a program containing business logic written by a Developer as per the application's needs. It works with the event bus, any change in entity triggers the event, and all the rules hooked to the event bus are executed sequentially. Rules are reusable objects across client, server, and middleware. Rules are reusable and hence can be subscribed multiple times with different Channel types or other combinations. Entity Rule Creation:​ Step 1: Go to the Rule tab and click on the add icon(+). Field Description Event type Select the event type. Based on the type of event you choose rule will be executed. Type Select the channel type, based on this the transaction will be performed. Exit ID is an ID you put in for the rule subscription. (can select from the existing one). Clazz This will be the rule file name. Invocation Method The method needs to be called. Step 2: Select the Event Type from the drop-down. The event type will mention when the rules will be executed. Event types: Endpoint resolver (Once the rule is being executed in-between it picks Endpoint Resolver and resolves it or whenever the online save is going to the klarion server Endpoint resolver will get called) On Create ( rule will be executed on create of an entity) On Delete (rule will be executed on delete of an entity) On Update (rule will be executed on update of an entity) Step 3: Select the channel type(there are different input channels to perform a transaction on an entity, channel type selection decides when to trigger the Rule). Channel Type: Endpoint / Device on Klarion server- always on the client Endpoint / Device on Klarion server Endpoint / Device on Klarion server- always on server Endpoint / Device to Server/ Client -Network Context Switch Legacy on Klarion server Klarion server to Klarion offline server Klarion server to Klarion Server Step 4: Fill in the value for Exit ID. Exit ID: It's an ID that you put in for the rule subscription. (can select from the existing one). Step 5: In the Clazz field provide the rule file name (example: rules/<file_name>) and in the invocation method provide an event name. You will be using that event to write your business logic codes. NOTE: If you are creating a Rule for the same entity you can fill this inside the Clazz field. Step 6: Click on the save button to save the newly created rule. Note: The last column drop-down icon has two fields(Choose Existing and Create New) Choose Existing: This will list down all the existing rules for that entity. You directly select it and use it. Create New: Create New will clear some fields from the created rule fields. For more information, please refer to the training guide. 2.2.2. Query Detail​ On selection of any query in the tree, it will display all available options in the detail section. The description of each tab is given below: 2.2.2.1. Detail​ This tab will list all the basic information related to the query. It contains fields like return entity, DB Selection, Select distinct, app mode, Tenant level, query type and expand all. The description of each of the fields is given below: Return Entity:​ Return entity indicates the return type of the query. The second field of the return entity is the Alias of that entity. Transient Entity (Aggregate Queries)​ In the case of aggregate queries and native aggregate queries, an additional field called Transient Entity is present. In the Procify Page Builder, Page Data Model will be created from the Transient Entity rather than the return entity. The Transient Entity will include all the properties from the SELECT clause, ensuring that all values are properly displayed on the screen. Differences Between Aggregate and Native Aggregate Queries Aggregate query automatically generates a transient entity containing all properties used in the SELECT clause. If no SELECT clause is modeled, the return entity is used instead. Properties added automatically by the framework to the transient entity cannot be deleted. However, users can add their own properties to the transient entity for additional calculations, display purposes, or other operations. Native aggregate queries require the user to explicitly create a transient entity and assign it to the “Transient Entity” in the detail tab of the query. All aliases must be included as properties; if no alias is provided, the property name from the Entity should be included in the query. Note: For native aggregate queries, if a transient entity is not specified manually, it will be defaulted to the return entity. DB Selection:​ We have two DB instances, one is Reader and another is Writer, where Writer is RunTimeMain and Reader is RunTimeSecondary. We can shift the load of a particular query to the Reader instance by maintaining the proper DB Selection. By default it runs on RunTimeMain. In case of RunTimeSecondary, if we are updating some property of the entityset it will persist via RunTimeMain. Select Distinct:​ This field specifies whether the query created will be giving unique records or not. Select Distinct returns unique records based on the specified columns. If the selected columns are not primary keys, and loadAll is false, the distinction is made based on the primary key, which might still include duplicates. To ensure distinctness based on the selected columns, loadAll must be set to true. App Mode:​ App mode refers to the network mode of the entity. This is similar to what we get in identity-level app mode. Click here to read about supported app modes in detail. Tenant Level:​ This radio button allows you to make the dependent or independent. Query Type:​ Query supports multiple types of query modelling which are easy to define and use in the application. Based on the application scenario and use case, the query type has to be decided. Runtime Query ( former Entity Query)​ Modelled Query (former Dynamic Query)​ Native Query (former Advanced Query)​ Aggregate Query (ReadOnly with Modelling support)​ Native Aggregate Query (ReadOnly with Raw SQl)​ Note: Changing modelled query to aggregate/native aggregate will trigger a dialog mentioning the warnings which have to resolved depending on the developer’s need. On click of Open Where Used List, a dialog will appear mentioning if any screen is created using the query. Query Modelling​ Update:​ This will update the SQL query generated as per the data maintained for the query. Expand All:​ The “Expand All” text area contains all the relations for which the data will be loaded during the parent query execution.Currently, ExpandAll does not work when an INNER JOIN is used in a query, as we do not support the combination of ExpandAll and INNER JOIN together. Note: Expand All is not supported for aggregate queries. When a query uses aggregate functions (like SUM, COUNT, AVG, etc.), it consolidates multiple rows into summary values. Because of this aggregation, the original row-level detail is lost. Expand All relies on accessing these underlying row-level relations to fetch related data. Since the individual rows no longer exist in the aggregated result, it is not possible to expand relations in this context. Expand All with Joins: The Expand All feature is supported in queries that include joins. Joins defined in the parent query are automatically appended during Expand All execution. Entity Restrictions: The same entity cannot be used simultaneously in both the main query and in the Expand All clause. This restriction helps avoid circular references and data redundancy. Where Conditions on Joined Entities: You can apply WHERE conditions on secondary (joined) entities in queries that use Expand All. This is considered while filtering of expanded data. Note:Supported Functionality (BOL_ Version 7-2-113 and onwards) 2.2.2.2. Entities And Join​ In this tab, we can manually add the joins and choose join types. We can also manually select the fields and can group/order the fields. In the Entity Join section of our queries, we can now incorporate fixed values such as 100, 200, 'RAM', 'Rincy', 'Karan', as well as system variables like $SYSTEM.userID and $SYSTEM.now within the join conditions. Note:To ensure uniqueness in the results, we enable the SELECT DISTINCT option. Below are the details of the fields shown above in the image Entity:​ This field is for root entities. The entity to which we are applying the Joins. Description: A short description for entity join Join Type: A JOIN clause is used to combine rows from two or more tables. There are four types of join. 2.2.2.3. Select Properties​ This tab contains information about properties in the select clause. All the properties present in the query will be listed here. Unlike modeled queries, aggregate queries allow the same property to be included multiple times with different aggregation functions. For example: Counting the number of cities and also listing the names of the cities. Calculating the minimum, maximum, and average values of a property such as marks. Note: Each aggregated instance of a property must have a unique alias to ensure that all values are displayed correctly in the query result. All the fields of this screen are described below: Entity​ Entity name of the selected property. Property​ Entity property ID which is present in the query. Description​ A short description of the query. Key Attributes​ This field represents whether the respective property is primary, mandatory, or has an id-series or not. Click here to learn more about each of these. Alias​ Alias refers to the SQL aliases used to give a table, or a column in a table, a temporary name. Aggregation​ Aggregation in a query refers to the process of combining multiple rows of data into a single summary value. It is commonly used to calculate metrics such as sum, average, count, maximum, minimum, or other summary statistics. Note: When using a modeled query, it is recommended to provide an alias to display the aggregated value on the screen. This can be done either by creating a transient property or by using an existing property. Or the count_of_property or other aggregated result returned by the database may not appear in the transient node or returned entity. Additional Note: When performing aggregation within an aggregate query, an alias is automatically generated. However, it can also be manually specified if desired. 2.2.2.4. Parameters​ This tab lists all the query properties that are created under this query. A query property is similar to what an entity is having but this property will be used only in the runtime and no actual attributes will be added in the database table. Below is the definition of the fields shown above in the image: Query Property ID:​ Provide the ID for query property (should only contain small chars, numerical, ‘_’). This is the unique key used for accessing the specified query property. Short Label:​ Mention the label which is required to be shown in the UI when using search or any other function. Default Value:​ When providing default value in a query property it will act as a predefined value for that property and when the query will be executed it will prefill the query property with the provided default value. Description: A short description of the query property. Property Type:​ Property Type is generated in association with the query ID. This also refers to the element ID. Domain:​ It shows the data type for the query property. This generally means what will be the data type of the property specified like String, Int, Boolean, etc. Length:​ This field will display the length of the field specified. For example: For String it can have a Length 255 or 32; For Integer it can have a length of 16,32 or 64 etc. 2.2.2.5. Where​ Where the tab contains all the conditional data present in the query. To use the where clause, follow these steps: Step 1: Go to the Where tab and click on Add icon(+) Step 2: Fill the fields according to your requirements. Step 3: Click on save button 2.2.2.6. Group By​ Group by tab contains all the properties present in the group by clause. To use a group, follow these steps: Step 1: Go to group by tab and click on add icon(+) Step 2: Select the field from vh on which you want to apply group by Step 3: Click on the save button 2.2.2.7. Having​ The Having tab will list down all the properties present in the having clause. To use having on an entity property follow the same steps as we followed in the Where clause 2.2.2.8. Sort Order​ Sort order is used to sort the property in either ascending or descending order. The fields are explained below: Field:​ It refers to the property for which a sort order has been created. Order:​ Order specifies whether the data will be sorted in ascending or descending order. Note: To use sort order on any property, go to the sort order tab and inside that tab click on the add icon(+) fill in the data for your requirement and click on the save button. 2.2.2.9. Expand All​ The “Expand All” tab contains all the relations in one place for which the data will be loaded during the parent query execution. Note: In all the above sections listed, you can add and delete properties as and when required. The option for the same is given in all the sections. 2.2.3 Value Help Detail​ This tab contains all the details about the value help. Value Help:​ In the Application, ID/key is frequently used to store the related data and at the same time in the user interface descriptive explanation is required. To achieve this, the ID/key is represented by other single/multiple data from the related table. Value help is also used to supply the choices available to fill (combo, dropdown, auto-complete) as selection data. Value help can restrict accepting the input value from valid sets. VH_TRANSACTION​ VH Transaction is a common ValueHelp functionality provided by KloBase which can fulfil most of the basic requirements in the application. Icon:​ It is used in case we want to add an icon for any of the value help. Entity/Query:​ This will display the entity/query name associated with this value help. Desc Format:​ Desc format of a value help defines how the value help should be formatted and displayed.
