All the page Area ID(s) provided in the page’s layout section will implement the master-detail-detail paradigm by displaying up to three pages (page Areas) in separate columns. For a Flexible column layout, only three columns will be rendered, if more than three layout containers are provided in the layout section it will take the first three layout containers/sections. Configuration:​ For using the flexible column layout, select the screenType of a pageLayout as flexi_column. In the layout section of that pageLayout add the layouts. The setLayout() method was used in Flexible Column to define the layout width. As Flexible Column is now deprecated, it is recommended to use setFirstColumnWidth() in pagelayout type Two Column to configure column widths. Example: Flexible_col one Column Expanded Flexible_col two Column Expanded Flexible_col three Column Expanded

documents.t: It is similar to a flexible column. The only difference is that it can only implement the master-detail paradigm up to two pages only. And also unlike a flexible column it provides a horizontal splitter between the two pages.. Configuration:​ For using the two column layout, select the screenType of a pageLayout as two_column. Assign pages and sections. Use setFirstColumnWidth() to configure column widths. two_column one Column Expanded two_column two Column Expanded

Stack is a layout structure where the required elements show up one by one on a particular action based on the given metadata. Configuration:​ For using the stack layout, select the screenType of pageLayout / PageArea as stack. Example: We have a pageLayout of screentype stack: Stack will render only one layoutSubscreen at a time. As a default, the first layoutSubscreen is rendered. When it is navigated to the second layoutsubscreen it hides the first one & displays the pageArea it is navigated to.

Tab Layout represents a collection of tabs with associated content. The number of tabs rendered will be equal to the number of section/section container ID(s) given in the layout Data section. The tab title will be taken from the section/page Area’s title property, the tab title will only be visible if the flags are maintained in the layout data section and the showTitle property is marked as true. Configuration:​ For using the tab layout, select the screenType of pageLayout / PageArea as tab. In the detail section, mark the showTitle as true. After adding the showTitle as true, in the layout section. For the layouts added (pageArea / section ) add the property showTitle and title, provide the values. Note: selectedKey reflects the currently active tab/section — it is not a one-time "default tab" setting. If bound to a data field, the Tab control will always show whichever tab that field currently holds, and will keep showing it on subsequent loads/refreshes unless the field's value is explicitly reset. If the supplied key doesn't match any tab/section currently rendered, the control falls back to another available tab instead of forcing the configured one. To always land users on the same section regardless of prior state, drive it explicitly through navigation rather than relying on selectedKey alone. 12.4.1. documents.t: onPageInit​ onPageInit hook method will be called only once as soon as the controller is loaded The transaction, model , and the UI is yet to be created for this, so those will not be available in this method. onPageModelReady​ onPageModelReady event will be called when the model is created and the transnodes are initialized, but the data is not set to the model yet. From this hook method developer can call skipModelPreparation method which will skip setting the data and executing the query. If the developer skips the model preparation, then developer should be responsible for setting the data is the model onPageEnter​ onPageEnter hook method will be called whenever the page enters the visible area by means of navigation(both forward and backward navigation). If the navigation is within the same page, this method will not be triggered onPageExit:​ onPageExit hook method will be called in the source page whenever the user navigates to a different page onPageDestroy: onPageDestroy hook method will be called only once when the page is destroyed. Page will be destroyed during the back navigation Example : if you are navigating back from PageB to pageA then PageB will be destroyed 14.1.1. TransNode API:​ Refer to this link for TransNode API. 14.1.2. Navigation API:​ Refer to this link for navigation API.

onValidate:​ If the transNode’s onarrive (in the transNode’s detail section) is provided as valid then, onValidate will be called during navigation. onAfterCreate:​ onAfterCreate method will be called once the new entity is created. onDelete:​ The onDelete method will be called once the entity is deleted.

Setter function will be called once the entity property value is changed. Example: public set firstName(new\_value:string){ if(new\_value \== this.firstName) return; this.name:string \= new\_value\+" "\+this.lastName; this.s("firstName",new\_value,"string",false,false); } Getter function will be called whenever the entity property is getting read. Example: public get name():string{ return this.Firstname \+" "\+this.lastName }

The Where Used list can be accessed from the context menu of the following elements: Page Page Area Section Transnode To open the Where Used dialog: Right-click on the required element (Page, Page Area, Section, or Transnode). The context menu is displayed. Select Show Where Used from the menu. The Where Used dialog opens, displaying all references for the selected element. ​ When clicking on Show Where Used from the context menu, a Where Used dialog box opens. This dialog displays all references to the selected item within the current application. Dialog Layout​ The Where Used dialog is divided into two sections: Left Panel (Tree View) Displays a hierarchical list of all references for the selected item. Right Panel (Details View) Shows detailed information for the reference selected in the left panel. Selecting an entry in the tree view updates the details shown in the right panel. Supported Elements​ The Where Used feature is available for the following elements: Pages Page Areas Sections Transnodes Reference Checks by Element Type​ Pages The system checks for references in: Application menus Home pages Other pages (including embedded sections and tags) Associated files (controllers, utils) Navigation events within the current page (for example, navTo events) Page Areas The system checks for references in: Associated files(controllers, utils) NavTo Events, layouts in other pages and the current page Transnodes The system checks for references in: Binded data paths Associated files(controllers, utils) Navigating to Referenced Objects​ The Where Used dialog allows direct navigation to referenced application objects. In the left tree section, a Navigate button is displayed for application-level objects. When you click this button: A new tab opens automatically. The relevant tool or editor is loaded. The referenced object is preselected and highlighted in the opened tool.

For Grid, Tree, and Auto Grid section types, the Builder automatically applies horizontal alignment (hAlign) and text align property based on the control type and its associated binding. So the column header and the control will be aligned as per the standards based on the domain and control type Numeric Field Alignment​ If a control is bound to a property whose domain type is Integer or Decimal, the Builder automatically adds the hAlign config property and textAlign control property with the value Right. This automatic alignment is applied only when: The control is an input-based control. The control is bound to a property of domain type Integer or Decimal. Alignment Updates on Control Changes​ During updates, if: A control's value property or dsrc is modified, or A new binding is added to the control, the Builder automatically detects the bound property and updates the alignment accordingly.

For the Mobile view, the default alignment behavior is retained and no automatic alignment adjustments are applied.
